# Arduino board targets — CircuitForge 0.33

Supported: Uno R3, classic Nano, Pro Mini 5 V / 16 MHz, Mega2560 R3, Duemilanove ATmega328P, Arduino Pro 5 V / 16 MHz. Each project supports one MCU. ATmega168 and 3.3 V / 8 MHz Pro variants are separate targets and are not advertised here.

## Mega2560

The physical definition follows [Arduino's full pinout](https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/pinouts/A000067-full-pinout.pdf) and the pinned Arduino AVR 1.8.7 Mega variant. D0–D53 and A0–A15 map to ports A/B/C/D/E/F/G/H/J/K/L. Runtime digital aliases D54–D69 resolve to A0–A15; editor endpoints retain printed A names. SDA/SCL pads alias D20/D21. Ground and 5 V pads are joined canonically; IOREF aliases 5 V. A6/A7 on Mega remain full GPIO, unlike classic Nano/Pro Mini's analog-only pads.

The CPU executes AVR instructions with 262144-byte flash, three-byte PC and SRAM 0x200–0x21ff. Application limits are 253952 flash bytes and 8192 static SRAM bytes; stack/heap remain runtime responsibilities. Compiler macros, avr6 code generation, variant headers, CRT, linker data origin and libraries match this MCU. Intel HEX/import/history validation uses the selected target capacity.

Six timers drive all 15 Arduino PWM pads: D2–D13, D44–D46. External IRQs follow Arduino D2/D3/D18/D19/D20/D21 mapping. PCINT groups include PB, shared PE0/PJ and PK. Tests exercise all six external interrupts and all three PCINT groups, plus all 15 PWM outputs and native pulseIn assembly measuring a physically jumpered Timer3 waveform.

Bus adapters resolve actual electrical connections: Wire on D20/D21, SPI MOSI51/MISO50/SCK52/SS53, USART0 RX0/TX1, USART1 RX19/TX18, USART2 RX17/TX16 and USART3 RX15/TX14. The terminal selector maintains independent bounded output histories and sends through the selected receiver. UART RX completes at the final stop-bit sample, so adjacent start bits cannot be missed at a same-cycle boundary. Binary sensor frames, bad wiring/power/format and physical UART edges retain existing behavior.

Examples: Mega A15/pot/Timer5/3KB SRAM; Serial1 MH-Z19B; SHT31 I2C; MCP3008 SPI; Duemilanove and Arduino Pro A0/A5/PWM. All six sources have genuine GCC WASM HEX cache and source/board fingerprints. High-numbered logic channels and differential measurement probes survive JSON/ZIP and worker reset.

## Toolchain and drawings

Pinned compiler WASM remains @horang-corp/avr-gcc-wasm 0.2.0 from the upstream CDN. `mega-toolchain/` supplies target-specific native avr6 core/runtime/link objects and the Mega variant, rebuilt from retained original sources. Read its README and FIRMWARE-NOTICES.md for licenses, SHA256 manifest and reproducible preparation commands. Debug sections are stripped; exported symbols/code remain available for relinking modified sources. Wire/SPI/SoftwareSerial and the selected Adafruit GFX/BusIO/SSD1306 stack are supported by the existing library selection.

Mega, Duemilanove and Pro SVGs are original CC0 illustrations regenerated by scripts/draw-expanded-boards.mjs. Pin coordinate definitions drive both pad hit targets and drawings. Decorative USB/FTDI circuitry is not a USB/bootloader emulation. The board's ideal 5 V / 3.3 V rails retain the existing DC supply model; no VIN regulator, thermal or damage model is claimed. ADC alternate references/differential modes, watchdog, EEPROM, USB firmware and JTAG are outside accepted coverage. Timer acceptance covers Arduino PWM and millis/pulse timing, not every custom timer mode.

## Verification

npm run build; npm test. Rebuild relevant GCC fixtures with scripts/check-mega-projects.mjs, check-mega-browser.mjs, check-mega-irq.mjs, check-mega-pwm.mjs, check-mega-pulse.mjs. Browser acceptance includes real GCC compilation, A15=512, SRAM3208/8192, all four terminal ports, Serial1_CO2=800, SHT T=25.00 RH=50.00, MCP CH0=614, and both additional 328P cards. check-mega-browser.mjs also links/executes 152382-byte firmware across the 128KB far-flash boundary and links selected Adafruit/Wire/SPI libraries.
